name: Ring L-Sit
steps: Set the rings a little above the floor and jump into support with locked arms.
Push down hard on the rings and lock your shoulders.
Lift your legs until they are straight out in front of you.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, with your toes pointed.
Bend your knees to come out of it before your form breaks.

name: Ring Support Hold
steps: Grip the rings and jump into support with your arms locked.
Turn the rings out so your palms face forward.
Pull your shoulders down and squeeze your glutes and abs.
Hold still, without letting the rings wobble or drift.
Step down before the shake gets the better of you.

name: Ring Muscle-Up
steps: Hang from the rings with a false grip, wrists over the rings.
Pull explosively, bringing the rings to your chest.
Lean forward and roll your shoulders over the rings as you pass them.
Press out of the dip until your arms are locked in support.
Come down the same way, under control, one step at a time.

name: Plank
steps: Set your forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body is one straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs.
Keep your hips level, neither sagging nor piked up.
Breathe steadily and hold for the time you set.

name: Bench Leg Raise
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your legs hanging off the end from the knees down.
Hold the sides of the bench behind your head or tuck your hands under your hips.
Lift your legs a few centimetres off the bench with your feet together.
Raise your straight legs until they are almost vertical.
Lower them slowly without letting them touch the bench.

name: Side Plank
steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and your legs stacked.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Keep your top hip stacked over the bottom one without rolling forward.
Hold, breathing steadily, then switch sides.

name: Cross-Body Crunch
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands lightly beside your head.
Curl up and twist to bring one elbow towards the opposite knee.
Squeeze your abs as the elbow and knee meet.
Lower back down and repeat on the other side.

name: Dead Hang
steps: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms.
Let your shoulders stretch while keeping a light brace in your abs.
Hold for the time you set, then step down under control.

name: Outdoor Run
steps: Start with five minutes of easy jogging to warm up.
Run tall, with relaxed shoulders and a slight forward lean.
Land under your hips with short, quick steps.
Keep a pace you could hold a conversation at, unless it is an interval day.
Finish with a few minutes of walking.

name: Outdoor Cycling
steps: Set the saddle so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of each pedal stroke.
Start in an easy gear for the first few minutes.
Keep a smooth cadence instead of mashing the pedals.
Shift early on climbs to keep the effort steady.

name: Walk
steps: Walk tall with your shoulders relaxed and your arms swinging.
Roll through each step from heel to toe.
Pick a pace that raises your breathing without leaving you out of breath.

name: Hiking
steps: Wear shoes with good grip and bring water.
Shorten your stride on steep climbs and keep a steady rhythm.
Lean slightly into the slope going up and bend your knees going down.
Take short breaks before you are exhausted, not after.

name: Swimming
steps: Warm up with a few easy lengths.
Keep your body long and flat, with your head in line with your spine.
Reach forward on each stroke and pull the water back past your hips.
Breathe to the side in rhythm with your strokes.
Log the total distance and the time you spent swimming.

name: Football
steps: Warm up with easy jogging and a few sprints.
Log the minutes you played, not the time at the pitch.
Add the distance if your watch tracked it.

name: Basketball
steps: Warm up your ankles and do a few jumps first.
Log the minutes you were on the court.
Count shooting practice as a separate, easier session.

name: Volleyball
steps: Warm up your shoulders and do a few jumps first.
Log the minutes of play.
Beach volleyball counts too: the sand makes it harder.

name: Tennis
steps: Warm up your shoulder and wrist before the first serve.
Log the minutes you played.
Rallies count; long breaks between sets do not.

name: Padel
steps: Warm up your shoulder, wrist and ankles.
Log the minutes of play.
Doubles or singles, it all counts.

name: Badminton
steps: Warm up your shoulder and do a few lunges.
Log the minutes of play.
Short, fast rallies make it real cardio.

name: Squash
steps: Warm up well: squash is fast from the first point.
Log the minutes you played.
Drink water between games.

name: Table Tennis
steps: Loosen your wrist and shoulder first.
Log the minutes of play.
Stay on the balls of your feet between shots.

name: Handball
steps: Warm up your throwing shoulder and do a few sprints.
Log the minutes you played.
Add the distance if your watch tracked it.

name: Rugby
steps: Warm up with jogging, sprints and shoulder mobility.
Log the minutes you played or trained.
Contact days are hard on recovery: plan an easier gym day after.

name: Boxing
steps: Warm up with jump rope and shadow boxing.
Log the minutes of rounds and bag work.
Keep your hands up and breathe out on each punch.

name: Martial Arts
steps: Warm up your hips, shoulders and neck.
Log the minutes of class or sparring.
Rolling and sparring count; long talks between drills do not.

name: Climbing
steps: Warm up on easy routes first.
Log the minutes you spent climbing.
Rest your fingers: hard climbing days stress the same muscles as pulling in the gym.

name: Skiing
steps: Warm up your legs and hips before the first run.
Log the minutes you were actually skiing.
Add the distance if your watch tracked it.

name: Surfing
steps: Warm up your shoulders before you paddle out.
Log the minutes you were in the water.
Paddling is most of the work: it trains your back and shoulders.

name: Dance
steps: Start with a few easy songs to warm up.
Log the minutes you danced.
Classes and nights out both count.

name: Golf
steps: Loosen your back and hips before the first swing.
Log the minutes you played.
Walking the course adds a lot: add the distance if you tracked it.

name: Leg Extension
steps: Adjust the backrest and ensure the machine axis of rotation aligns directly with the lateral side of your knee joint.
Grasp the side handles firmly, pull yourself down into the seat, and engage your core to lock your hips and pelvis in place.
Exhale as you extend your legs upward in a smooth, controlled motion by contracting your quadriceps.
Hold the fully extended position for 1–2 seconds at the top of the movement.
Inhale as you slowly lower the weight back to the starting position over a 2- to 3-second cadence.

name: Yuri's Shoulder Band Warmup
steps: Hold a light band overhead with your arms straight and your hands wider than your shoulders.
Pull the band apart and take your arms back and down behind you until they reach your hips.
Bring the band back overhead along the same path, keeping your elbows locked.
Widen your grip if your shoulders pinch, and narrow it as the movement gets easier.
Work through the whole sequence before you start the session.

name: Wrist Prep
steps: Kneel with your palms flat on the floor and your fingers pointing forward.
Rock your weight gently forward and back to open the front of your wrists.
Turn your hands so the fingers point back towards your knees and rock again.
Flip onto the backs of your hands and press down lightly.
Finish with slow fist circles in both directions to warm the joint.

name: Arch Hang
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you.
Pull your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Squeeze your glutes and push your chest through so your body forms an arch.
Look forward and keep your legs straight and together.
Hold the arch for as long as the routine asks for.

name: Parallel Bar Support Hold
steps: Grip the parallel bars and press yourself up to straight arms.
Lock your elbows and push the bars down to lift your shoulders away from your ears.
Keep your body upright with your legs straight and together.
Brace your core so your hips stay still.
Hold the position for as long as the routine asks for.

name: Smith Upright Row
steps: Set the Smith bar at arm's length in front of your thighs.
Take the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar up along your body towards your chin, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your elbows reach shoulder height and squeeze your shoulders.
Lower the bar slowly back to your thighs.

name: Cable Upright Row
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand close to the stack.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip in front of your thighs.
Keep your back straight and your abs tight.
Pull the bar up to shoulder height, leading with your elbows.
Lower the bar under control back to your thighs.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Turn your palms towards your body and keep your abs tight.
Raise the dumbbells towards your shoulders by lifting your elbows out to the sides.
Stop when your elbows reach shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to your thighs.

name: Band Upright Row
steps: Stand on the middle of a band and hold one end in each hand.
Keep your back straight and your abs drawn in.
Pull your hands up towards your collarbone, lifting your elbows out wide.
Stop when your elbows are level with your shoulders.
Lower your hands slowly back to your thighs.

name: Cable Bent-over Rear Delt Raise
steps: Hold the handle of a low pulley in one hand and step away from the stack.
Hinge forward until your chest is almost parallel to the floor.
Rest your free hand on your thigh and let the working arm hang.
Raise the arm out to the side until it is level with your shoulder.
Lower it slowly and switch arms after the set.

name: Band Reverse Fly
steps: Anchor a band to a post at chest height and hold one end in each hand.
Step back until the band is tight with your arms straight in front of you.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your knees soft.
Open your arms out to the sides until they line up with your shoulders.
Bring your hands back together in front of your chest slowly.

name: Lying Rear Lateral Raise
steps: Lie face down on a raised bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang below the bench with your elbows slightly bent.
Keep your toes on the floor to stay steady.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides up to shoulder height.
Lower them slowly until your arms hang down again.

name: Cable Internal Rotation
steps: Sit on the floor side-on to a low pulley with your legs out in front.
Hold the handle with the arm nearest the stack, elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your elbow tucked against your side the whole time.
Rotate your forearm across your stomach without moving the elbow.
Let the handle return slowly and switch sides after the set.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your abs tight.
Hold one dumbbell at shoulder height with your elbow bent.
Press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is fully extended.
Keep your torso upright without leaning to the side.
Lower the dumbbell back to your shoulder and switch arms after the set.

name: Assisted Squat
steps: Hold a door frame, a pole or a suspension strap at arm length.
Stand with your feet a little wider than your shoulders.
Sit back and down, using your hands only as much as you need.
Go as deep as you can while keeping your heels on the floor.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
steps: Stand a stride in front of a bench or a chair.
Rest the top of your back foot on it behind you.
Lower straight down until your back knee almost touches the floor.
Keep your chest tall and your front shin close to vertical.
Push through the front heel to stand back up.

name: Beginner Shrimp Squat
steps: Stand on one leg with the other knee bent and that foot lifted behind you.
Reach both arms forward for balance instead of holding the back foot.
Lower yourself until the back knee and the toes of that foot rest on the floor.
Keep your standing heel down and your chest up throughout.
Drive through the standing leg to come back to standing.

name: Intermediate Shrimp Squat
steps: Stand on one leg and hold the other foot behind you with the same-side hand.
Reach your free arm forward to help you balance.
Lower yourself until the back knee touches the floor.
Let your chest lean forward as far as you need to stay over the standing foot.
Push back up without letting the back foot touch down.

name: Weighted Shrimp Squat
steps: Wear a weighted vest or hold a plate against your chest with your free hand.
Stand on one leg and hold the other foot behind you with the same-side hand.
Lower yourself under control until the back knee touches the floor.
Keep your chest up and your standing heel flat on the floor.
Push back up to standing without letting the back foot touch down.

name: Barbell Lunge
steps: Rest a barbell across your upper back with a grip wider than your shoulders.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your chest up.
Take a long step forward with one leg.
Lower your back knee until it is just above the floor.
Push through the front heel to step back and switch legs.

name: Barbell Reverse Lunge
steps: Take a barbell from the rack onto your upper back.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your abs tight.
Step back with one leg and lower your back knee towards the floor.
Keep your front shin upright and your chest tall.
Drive through the front foot to return and switch legs.

name: Dumbbell Squat
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than your shoulders and a dumbbell in each hand.
Let the dumbbells hang at your sides with your arms straight.
Sit your hips back and bend your knees as if sitting on a chair.
Go down as far as you can while keeping your heels on the floor.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.

name: Barbell Step-up
steps: Place a sturdy box or bench in front of you.
Rest a barbell across your upper back with a wide grip.
Step up with one foot and drive through that heel to stand on the box.
Step back down with the same leg first.
Finish the set and repeat leading with the other leg.

name: Hack Squat
steps: Step into the hack squat machine with your back and shoulders against the pads.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety handles and bend your knees to lower yourself.
Go down until your thighs are about parallel to the platform.
Push through your heels to straighten your legs without locking your knees.

name: Negative Dip
steps: Jump or step up to the top of the dip bars with straight arms.
Pull your shoulders down and keep your chest slightly forward.
Bend your elbows and lower yourself as slowly as you can, counting to three.
Stop when your shoulders drop below your elbows.
Step back up to the top and start the next rep.

name: Bodyweight Romanian Deadlift
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your thighs.
Keep a soft bend in your knees and your back flat.
Push your hips back and slide your hands down your legs.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the back of your thighs.
Squeeze your glutes to bring your hips back under you.

name: Bodyweight Single-Leg Deadlift
steps: Stand on one leg with a soft bend in that knee.
Hinge forward at the hip and let the free leg rise straight behind you.
Reach your hands towards the floor and keep your hips level.
Stop when your torso and back leg are almost parallel to the floor.
Squeeze the glute to stand back up without touching the free foot down.

name: Banded Nordic Curl Negative
steps: Kneel on a pad with your ankles held down by a partner or a heavy anchor.
Loop a band around your chest and anchor it above and behind you.
Keep your hips straight so your body makes one line from knees to shoulders.
Lower yourself forward as slowly as you can and let your hands catch you.
Push yourself back up with your arms and reset for the next rep.

name: Banded Nordic Curl
steps: Kneel on a pad with your ankles held down by a partner or a heavy anchor.
Loop a band around your chest and anchor it above and behind you.
Keep your hips straight and your glutes squeezed throughout.
Lower yourself forward under control as far as you can.
Pull yourself back up with your hamstrings and let the band help.

name: Nordic Curl
steps: Kneel on a pad with your ankles held down by a partner or a heavy anchor.
Keep your hips straight so your body makes one line from knees to shoulders.
Lower yourself forward as slowly as your hamstrings allow.
Keep your hands ready in front of you in case you drop.
Pull yourself back up to kneeling without bending at the hips.

name: Vertical Row

steps: Grab a door frame or a sturdy pole with both hands at chest height.
Stand close with your feet under your hands and your arms straight.
Lean back only slightly so your body stays nearly upright.
Pull your chest towards your hands and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Straighten your arms slowly to return to the start.

name: Incline Row
steps: Set a bar at about waist height, or use the edge of a sturdy table.
Take an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet forward so your body hangs at an angle, straight from head to heels.
Pull your chest to the bar and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself under control until your arms are straight.

name: Wide Row
steps: Set a bar at about waist height and lie underneath it.
Take an overhand grip much wider than your shoulders.
Keep your body straight from head to heels with your heels on the floor.
Pull your upper chest to the bar, leading with your elbows out to the sides.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again.

name: Weighted Inverted Row
steps: Set a bar at about waist height and lie underneath it.
Rest a weight plate on your chest or wear a weighted vest.
Keep your body straight from head to heels with your heels on the floor.
Pull your chest to the bar and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself under control until your arms are straight.

name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
steps: Sit at the pulldown with your thighs under the pad.
Grab the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Sit tall with your abs tight and your chest up.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
steps: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high pulley and step back from the stack.
Hold the bar with straight arms at about eye level.
Hinge forward slightly at the hips and brace your core.
Sweep the bar down to your thighs, keeping your arms straight.
Let the bar rise slowly back to eye level.

name: Pseudo Planche Push-up
steps: Set up in a push-up position with your hands beside your waist.
Turn your fingers out or back so your wrists stay comfortable.
Lean your shoulders forward past your hands and hold that lean.
Lower your chest to the floor without letting your hips drop.
Press back up while keeping the same forward lean.

name: Band Chest Fly
steps: Anchor a band to a post at chest height and face away from it.
Hold one end in each hand with your arms open to the sides.
Step forward until the band is tight.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest with a slight bend in the elbows.
Hold for a moment and open your arms back out slowly.

name: Flat Bench Cable Fly
steps: Place a flat bench between two low pulleys and lie on it.
Hold a handle in each hand with your arms open and palms facing up.
Keep your feet flat and your back against the bench.
Squeeze your chest to bring the handles together over your chest.
Lower your hands back to bench height slowly.

name: Incline Dumbbell Hammer Press
steps: Sit back on a bench set to about 45 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand.
Hold the dumbbells beside your chest with your palms facing each other.
Keep your feet flat and your back against the bench.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly back to the sides of your chest.

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
steps: Lie on a bench set to about 45 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand.
Press the dumbbells over your chest with your palms facing each other.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows for the whole set.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch.
Bring them back together over your chest along the same arc.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your feet planted and your abs tight.
Hold one dumbbell beside your chest.
Press the dumbbell up until your arm is straight.
Keep your hips and shoulders flat on the bench without twisting.
Lower it slowly and switch arms after the set.

name: Smith Incline Bench Press
steps: Set an incline bench at about 45 degrees inside the Smith machine.
Line the bench up so the bar comes down over your upper chest.
Grab the bar slightly wider than your shoulders and unlock it.
Lower the bar slowly to your upper chest without bouncing it.
Press the bar back up until your arms are straight.

name: Decline Chest Press Machine
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your lower chest.
Sit with your back against the pad and grab both handles.
Press the handles forward and down until your arms are almost straight.
Stop just short of locking your elbows.
Let the handles come back slowly to your chest.

name: Incline Chest Press Machine
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Sit with your back against the pad and grab both handles.
Press the handles forward and up until your arms are almost straight.
Stop just short of locking your elbows.
Let the handles come back slowly to your upper chest.

name: Barbell Reverse-Grip Bench Press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your feet planted on the floor.
Grab the bar with your palms facing your head, hands shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your lower chest.
Lower the bar slowly to your lower chest.
Press it back up until your arms are straight.
